claim: A default VPC is a logically isolated virtual network that AWS creates automatically for your account the first time you provision EC2 resources; an instance launched without a subnet ID goes into the default VPC.
question: What is a default VPC, and where does an instance go when you launch it without naming a subnet?

values.display: automatically created for your AWS account the first time you provision Amazon EC2 resources
values.spoken: AWS creates it for you automatically

values.display: When you launch an instance without specifying a subnet-ID, your instance will be launched in your default VPC
values.spoken: no subnet given means the default VPC

evidence.quote: A default VPC is a logically isolated virtual network in the AWS cloud that is automatically created for your AWS account the first time you provision Amazon EC2 resources. When you launch an instance without specifying a subnet-ID, your instance will be launched in your default VPC.

claim: AWS creates the default VPC with a default subnet in each Availability Zone of the Region, connects it to an internet gateway, and instances launched in it automatically receive public IP addresses.
question: Is a default VPC connected to the internet, and do its instances get public IP addresses?

values.display: a default subnet in each Availability Zone in the AWS region
values.spoken: one default subnet per Availability Zone

values.display: Your default VPC will be connected to an Internet gateway and your instances will automatically receive public IP addresses
values.spoken: internet gateway attached, public IPs by default

evidence.quote: AWS will automatically create a default VPC for you and will create a default subnet in each Availability Zone in the AWS region. Your default VPC will be connected to an Internet gateway and your instances will automatically receive public IP addresses, just like EC2-Classic.

claim: You can have one default VPC in each AWS Region where your Supported Platforms attribute is set to "EC2-VPC".

qualifiers.condition: Supported Platforms attribute set to EC2-VPC

evidence.quote: You can have one default VPC in each AWS region where your Supported Platforms attribute is set to "EC2-VPC".

claim: One default subnet is created for each Availability Zone in the default VPC.

values.display: One default subnet is created for each Availability Zone

evidence.quote: One default subnet is created for each Availability Zone in your default VPC.

claim: A default VPC is assigned the CIDR range 172.31.0.0/16, and its default subnets are /20 blocks within that range.

values.display: /20 netblocks

evidence.quote: Default VPCs are assigned a CIDR range of 172.31.0.0/16. Default subnets within a default VPC are assigned /20 netblocks within the VPC CIDR range.

claim: You can add nondefault subnets, such as private subnets, to a default VPC; to launch into one you target it with the console or the --subnet option of the CLI, API or SDK.
question: Can a default VPC have private subnets, and how do you launch into one?

values.display: target your launches using the console or the --subnet option from the CLI, API, or SDK

evidence.quote: Can I create additional subnets in my default VPC, such as private subnets?
Yes. To launch into nondefault subnets, you can target your launches using the console or the --subnet option from the CLI, API, or SDK.

note: The 'Yes' answers the FAQ heading 'Can I create additional subnets in my default VPC, such as private subnets?'; the quote itself only states how to launch into a nondefault subnet.

claim: You can delete a default VPC and later create a new default VPC from the console or CLI; the new one does not restore the deleted VPC.
question: Can you delete a default VPC, and can you get one back?

values.display: you can delete a default VPC
you can create a new default VPC directly from the VPC Console or by using the CLI
values.spoken: and create a new one from the console or CLI

values.display: This does not restore the previous VPC that was deleted
values.spoken: the old one is not restored

evidence.quote: Yes, you can delete a default VPC. Once deleted, you can create a new default VPC directly from the VPC Console or by using the CLI. This will create a new default VPC in the region. This does not restore the previous VPC that was deleted.

claim: You do not need a VPN connection to use a default VPC: default VPCs are attached to the internet, and all instances launched in default subnets automatically receive public IP addresses.
question: Do you need a VPN to use a default VPC?

values.display: Default VPCs are attached to the Internet and all instances launched in default subnets in the default VPC automatically receive public IP addresses
values.spoken: no; a default VPC is already on the internet

evidence.quote: No. Default VPCs are attached to the Internet and all instances launched in default subnets in the default VPC automatically receive public IP addresses. You can add a VPN connection to your default VPC if you choose.

claim: For IPv4, you can run any number of EC2 instances in a VPC as long as the VPC is sized to give each instance an IPv4 address; the FAQ adds that a /56 IPv6 VPC allows a virtually unlimited number of instances.
question: Is there a VPC limit on how many EC2 instances a VPC can hold?

values.display: any number of Amazon EC2 instances within a VPC, so long as your VPC is appropriately sized to have an IPv4 address assigned to each instance
values.spoken: as many as the address space allows

values.display: virtually unlimited number of Amazon EC2 instances

qualifiers.condition: IPv4: the VPC must be sized to give each instance an IPv4 address

evidence.quote: For instances that require IPv4 addressing, you can run any number of Amazon EC2 instances within a VPC, so long as your VPC is appropriately sized to have an IPv4 address assigned to each instance.
For IPv6 only instances, the VPC size of /56 provides you the ability to launch virtually unlimited number of Amazon EC2 instances.

note: The same FAQ answer still names an initial limit of 20 instances and a maximum VPC size of /16; EC2 now uses vCPU-based quotas, so that sentence is not adopted.

claim: Hosting several websites with separate IP addresses on one instance is not a good use of multiple network interfaces; AWS says to assign additional private IP addresses to the instance and associate Elastic IPs with them as needed.

values.spoken: extra private IPs plus Elastic IPs, not extra interfaces

evidence.quote: Yes, however, this is not a use case best suited for multiple interfaces. Instead, assign additional private IP addresses to the instance and then associate EIPs to the private IPs as needed.

claim: Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) is a managed service for planning, tracking and monitoring IP addresses for AWS workloads, and it can automate IP address assignment to VPCs.

values.display: a managed service that makes it easier for you to plan, track, and monitor IP addresses for your AWS workloads

evidence.quote: Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) is a managed service that makes it easier for you to plan, track, and monitor IP addresses for your AWS workloads.

claim: IPAM pools can be shared with other accounts in your AWS Organization through AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM), and also with accounts outside your primary Organization.

values.spoken: central monitoring and enforcement of traffic encryption

values.display: Monitor mode (for visibility, assessment and initiate migration) and Enforce mode (for preventing unencrypted traffic)

Monitor mode (for visibility, assessment and initiate migration) and Enforce mode (for preventing unencrypted traffic).

blocked from running instances that don’t support native nitro encryption

claim: You cannot switch an existing VPC straight to Enforce mode; you must first enable Monitor mode, identify non-compliant resources and create exclusions for them, and then switch to Enforce mode.

values.display: you must first
